subject: Hosted API: Capacity stacking proposal and throttle matrix for Q4 uplift
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@cartitude.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cartitude.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity — initial numbers and questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier. We ran the models against our busiest endpoints and have an initial ask: we expect 3.2x month-over-month growth for Q4 traffic (spikes at 5x during promotions).

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood provision a staged commit that starts at 2M tokens/day and ramps to 6M tokens/day over 60 days?
- What does the soft-throttle behavior look like at the 85% and 100% thresholds?
- Any recommendations for safe quantization or batching settings to keep latency sub-300ms for 512-token requests?

We have Procurement and Legal on copy to start the paperwork conversation. Attaching a short traffic extract.

Samir
Product Ops, Cartitude

Attachment: cartitude-q4-traffic-sample.csv (CSV)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cartitude.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity — initial numbers and questions

Samir — really appreciate the numbers and the spike scenarios. Short answers inline, then proposed next steps below.

- Staged commit: yes, we can structure a 60-day ramp. We typically model as a monthly committed throughput ladder (baseline commit + two ramp checkpoints). I sketched a 3-step ladder that meets your 2M -> 6M target while keeping unit price predictable.
- Soft-throttle behavior: at 85% we surface a pre-throttle warning in the Console and can enable burst credits to absorb spikes. At 100% we apply a fair-rate gate per API key and queue longer requests; we can also route non-critical traffic to a lower-cost model variant as fallback.
- Latency and batching: Karthik will run a quick perf matrix on your payload distribution. For 512-token requests we recommend 8-bit quantization on the large-encoder and a batch target of 4-8 to preserve sub-300ms p95 for single-region traffic.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Karthik validates latency estimates against your sample (target: 48h)
2) Ben to share a draft commercial (tiered commit ladder + burst pockets) — I attached our updated rate card draft.
3) Procurement/Legal to review and we’ll iterate on the PoC schedule (2-week PoC, then staged commit onboarding).

I attached the updated rate card and a draft throttle matrix for your team to review.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-updated-rate-card-2026-09-15.pdf (PDF), throttle-matrix-draft.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cartitude.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity — perf validation plan

Samir / Kimberly — I pulled the sample and ran a quick emulation on an n1-standard host pointing at our hosted endpoint with your payloads. Key notes: 
- Median payload length 420 tokens; 95th percentile 860 tokens (so 512 target will cover most but we should plan for tail).
- With batch target 6 and int8 quantization we saw p95 latency ~270ms in us-west region for 512-token synthetic runs.
- Cold-cache start (first few requests) adds ~120ms; KV prefix caching will reduce that after warm-up.

Recommendations:
- Use staged commit ladder: 60% baseline commit, 20% first ramp, 20% second ramp.
- Allocate a burst pocket equal to ~15% of peak expected daily tokens to avoid transient pre-throttles during promos.
- Implement prefix caching for your high-frequency templates and reduce model temperature for deterministic outputs (reduces token churn).

I also updated the throttle-matrix-draft.xlsx with gate thresholds and routing fallbacks (see column F for routing actions).

—Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

3) Any standard SLA credits if Redwood misses the monthly throughput SLO during onboarding?

If you can get a one-page commercial summary and a sample PO template by end of day Friday that would help unblock Legal.

Thanks,
Cartitude Procurement
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@cartitude.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@cartitude.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Hosted API commercial summary + PO template (Cartitude)

Team — attaching a one-page commercial summary and a sample PO template as requested. Quick bullets: 
- Billing cadence: monthly in arrears; if step-up occurs mid-month we prorate the commit charge for the remainder of that month and apply the new committed rate on the next invoice.
- Ladder effective rates (example):
  • Baseline commit (2M tokens/day): $0.0021 / token
  • Ramp 1 (4M tokens/day): $0.00185 / token
  • Ramp 2 (6M tokens/day): $0.0016 / token
- Burst pocket: billed at a higher overage rate but can be converted into committed tokens within 30 days if you choose; we typically reserve ~15% capacity for transient spikes.
- SLA credits: standard hosted SLA includes uptime SLOs; for throughput/commit misses during explicit onboarding windows we offer a one-time service credit negotiation (documented in the PO annex).

Next actions from Redwood:
1) Ben to upload the one-pager & PO to HubSpot (done) — link in thread.
2) Kimberly / Marissa to coordinate onboarding kickoff once Procurement confirms PO sign-off (target: 9/24 start for a 2-week PoC).
3) Karthik to run a final perf pass on staging with the exact PoC payloads (target: 9/22).

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
